findings.patch_old: A falsification-first research engine that turns questions into provenance-backed claims, executable kill tests, and auditable verdicts. ## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference - **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10 or newer. Standard library only: no network calls, no third-party packages. - **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**: ```bash python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ``` - **Try every mechanic in under 10 seconds** (from this folder): ```bash python -m engine demo python -m engine check python -m engine report r_000001 ``` `demo` builds a synthetic program with a source quote, a derived claim, a pre-registered hypothesis, a two-run kill test, a numeric verdict, and a transitive collapse. It is clearly labelled synthetic and makes no scientific claim. - **Start a real program**: ```bash python -m engine research add "My research" --scope "What this program is allowed to conclude" python -m engine question add r_000001 "Does mechanism M drive outcome O?" python -m engine source add r_000001 --title "Paper title" --year 2026 --doi 10.1000/example python -m engine claim add r_000001 --kind empirical --text "M covaries with O." \ --source s_000001 --quote "exact source sentence" --locator "Results, paragraph 2" \ --kill-test "A replicate where M rises and O falls." ```

findings.message: A snapshot whose export_digest contains a non-ASCII character makes hmac.compare_digest(str, str) raise TypeError, so export --check prints a traceback instead of reporting the file as altered.
A JSON line that is not an object (for example [1, 2]) makes record.get raise AttributeError, so a malformed snapshot crashes export --check instead of failing with the error triad.

initialize runs executescript(_SCHEMA) before reading schema_meta, so a database written by a newer schema has missing tables recreated before it is refused; the documented promise is that a newer version is refused without modification.
findings.patch_old:
def initialize(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict | None:
    """Create the schema, migrate an older one, and refuse a future version.

    Returns a migration report when an older database was upgraded, otherwise None, so a caller
    can tell the operator that upgrading changed what the gate will accept.
    """
    conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
findings.patch_new:
def initialize(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict | None:
    """Create the schema, migrate an older one, and refuse a future version.

    Returns a migration report when an older database was upgraded, otherwise None, so a caller
    can tell the operator that upgrading changed what the gate will accept.
    """
    existing = None
    if conn.execute(
        "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'schema_meta'"
    ).fetchone() is not None:
        existing = conn.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_meta").fetchone()
    if existing is not None and int(existing["version"]) > SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise EngineError(
            f"database schema version {int(existing['version'])} is newer than this build",
            f"this build reads schema version {SCHEMA_VERSION} only.",
            "use the engine version that wrote this database, or start a new database file.",
        )
    conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
